item.title: Is the U.S. Banking System Ready for a Post-Quantum Future?
item.description: Sultan Meghji argues that the hardest cryptographic deadline facing U.S. banks is being set by SWIFT and foreign supervisors, not Washington. Adversaries are harvesting encrypted financial traffic now. Three of the four fixes require no new statutory authority.

item.title: Don’t Slow Down AI Development—Speed Up Benchmarking
item.description: Ben Jensen and Yasir Atalan argue that the United States should stop debating how fast to build and start funding independent benchmarking—through NSF, NIST, and university policy labs.

item.title: The AI Industry Is Coalescing on “Pacing the Frontier.” Will It Actually Change Anything?
item.description: Over the past week, frontier labs, policymakers, and the U.S. public have reached remarkable consensus around calls to pace AI development. What now? Aalok Mehta outlines the four steps government and industry must take to translate the current moment into durable change.

item.title: CSIS Press Briefing: Previewing the Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) hosted a call-in press briefing to preview the upcoming Trump-Xi Summit.

item.title: Nuclear Statecraft: The Saudi Deal and U.S.-China Competition
item.description: The proposed U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear agreement has both risks and opportunities for U.S. national security. What would Washington gain? How might it affect global nonproliferation norms, or shape global interests in nuclear defense capacity? How might it impact U.S. competition with China?

item.title: What a Driver’s License Breach Shows About Foreign Data-AI Threats
item.description: A hacker advertised 153 million stolen driver's license images for sale. Far more than one breach, the incident exposes how foreign adversaries can amass and combine datasets and AI capabilities to build dossiers on Americans.

item.title: The Future of the Space Data Network: How the Pentagon Can Ensure a Competitive Marketplace
item.description: The Space Force must move quickly to build the Space Data Network, but speed should not come at the expense of competition. Matt Pearl examines how open standards, interoperability and vendor diversity can preserve strategic optionality and strengthen LEO satellite markets now.

item.title: AI Security Threats Aren’t a Hoax—But They Also Aren’t as Existential as They Might Seem
item.description: From a national security perspective, the abuses of AI outlined in Anthropic’s report aren’t especially new or surprising—in fact, they are consistent with how threat actors already behave, using AI to enhance the speed, scale, efficacy, and reach of their operations.

item.title: The Long Arm of China and North Korea’s Repression
item.description: CSIS' ongoing study found inmates in political prison camps are mobilized for manufacturing tied to Chinese orders. These abuses are not incidental; they sustain a partnership that reinforces North Korea's regime and its system of state control.

item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers September 16, 2026.
